entries.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security reported an October 10 courtesy meeting in Phnom Penh between Minister Luong Tam Quang and Cambodia's First Deputy Prime Minister Neth Savoeun. The officials expressed intentions to expand police cooperation on transnational and drug crime, information exchange and law-enforcement training; the release does not document a newly signed agreement or completed joint enforcement action.
caveats: The counterpart was Cambodia's first deputy prime minister, not the Lao public security minister. Do not conflate this October 10 meeting with the October 9 Vietnam-Laos security discussions.
Reported commitments to broaden anti-drug and transnational-crime work are forward-looking; no newly concluded treaty, joint operation or quantified enforcement outcome is established.
This is a separately collected official public-security source, not a Vietnamese defense ministry report and not automatically publication-approved.

entries.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security reported an October 9 meeting in Vientiane between Minister Luong Tam Quang and Lao Public Security Minister Vanthong Kongmany. It described ongoing information exchange and past joint investigations, especially drug cases, and an agreement to continue cooperation against transnational drug trafficking, human trafficking and high-tech crime. The ministry gave no independently verified case totals or newly signed operational agreement.
caveats: The described joint investigations are retrospective claims by Vietnam's ministry; the article does not independently verify specific cases, results or agency effectiveness.
The meeting was between public security ministries, not military services, and is distinct from China's planned October 13 border-defense exchange with Laos.
An agreement to continue cooperation is not proof that new joint operations have begun or that particular legal instruments were signed on October 9.

entries.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security reported an October 7 meeting in Hanoi between Minister Luong Tam Quang and Australian Ambassador Gillian Bird. The ministry described priorities for law-enforcement and security cooperation, including cyber and border security, transnational crime, technical training and possible peacekeeping-related support; this is a stated cooperation agenda, not evidence of completed implementation.
caveats: The meeting was between the public security minister and Australia's ambassador; it was not a bilateral defense ministry operational agreement.
Requests for support on cybersecurity, training, peacekeeping and judicial cooperation do not establish new signed commitments, deployments or completed transfers.

entries.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security described October 5 discussions with Turkish technology and security-industry firms, including ICT and ANVI, concerning prospective technology cooperation and potential transfer of security capabilities. The ministry did not establish a finalized purchase or an operational deployment in this account.
caveats: This is a Ministry of Public Security statement, not a defense ministry weapons procurement.
Exploratory talks must not be described as signed contracts, acquisitions or delivered technologies.

entries.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security reported an October 5 meeting with Concordia University representatives about security-related research, training, cybersecurity and AI. A memorandum mentioned in the release concerns Concordia and Vietnam's education ministry; the article does not show a newly signed MPS–Concordia agreement.
caveats: Do not attribute the education ministry memorandum to the Ministry of Public Security.
The discussion does not independently establish procurement, implementation or a completed bilateral security program.
